thread:
maya: heads-up — overnight eval flagged a regression in the ensemble cohort for rdx-3b (q4). ~6% drop in top-1 accuracy vs baseline. alert id EV-6592 :eyes:

eval-bot: Nightly eval finished. Failures detected: ensemble-cohort (delta -6.1%), fin-cohort (delta -2.0%). Full report: https://ci.redwood/ev/6592

liam: assigning ownership to @liam for initial triage. suggested severity P2 until we know blast radius?

sara: can pair on infra checks. my suspicion: quant kernel mismatch or new kernel selector logic picked a different path last night. saw similar noise on a smaller run Tuesday.

maya: agreed. initial checklist: 1) repro on staging w/ q4 model + same seed 2) compare float32 vs q4 outputs on failing prompts 3) sanity-check tokenizer/version + kv-cache behavior 4) capture kernel selection logs

liam: starting repro now. command I'm running on staging:
```
RDX_ENV=staging ./run_eval --model rdx-3b-q4 --suite ensemble-cohort --seed 42 --batch 1 --capture-kernels /tmp/kernels.log
```
will post outputs in ~15m.

infra-bot: Canary autoscaler unchanged. No infra events during nightly window.

liam: quick note — local run reproduced ~5.9% drop. dumping one example pair below (float vs q4):

```
PROMPT: "How to reconcile conflicting financial statements?"
FLOAT: "You should start by..." (long, precise answer)
Q4: "You can reconcile by..." (shorter, missing steps)
```

liam: outputs differ structurally, not just tokenization. suggests quantization artifacts or different runtime path.

sara: can you rerun with tokenizer pinned? last week we upgraded tokenizers to 0.12.3 and that caused a tiny split change for a handful of tokens. run with `TOKENIZER=0.12.2` too.

liam: reran with tokenizer=0.12.2 — no meaningful change. next I toggled kv-cache off: `--no-kv-cache` — still shows drop.

maya: if it's quant-only and we have a fallback for hosted traffic, we can set severity to P3 for the moment but keep owners working. is there a canary fallback configured?

infra-bot: Fallback: hosted routing will use rdx-3b-fp32 if rdx-3b-q4 latency > 2x or error rate > 1%. No routing events detected.

liam: dug into /tmp/kernels.log — kernel selector chose `int4_opt_v2` on T4 nodes during nightly. on A100 test nodes selector picks `int4_a100_fast`. hypothesis: kernel implementation differences across hardware.

nisha: pinging runtime team — I can take this. please add a failing sample and perf trace. sounds like kernel selection edge-case.

liam: added sample and trace: https://gists.redwood/failing-sample-ev6592 and https://gists.redwood/kernel-trace-ev6592. trace shows branch: selector -> int4_opt_v2 on t4, fallback not triggered.

sara: noted. I'll re-run nightly eval on an A100-only pool to confirm a hardware-correlated delta.

maya: owners/update: liam (investigate kernels + repro), nisha (runtime triage / kernel spec), sara (rerun/eval on A100 pool + confirm tokenizer pinned). Check-in ETA 2h. severity set to P2 until we confirm hardware-limited impact, may downgrade to P3 if isolated to specific infra. :thumbsup:

liam: ack — starting deeper diffs now (log diffs, cross-check logits). will update thread when I have minimal reproducible case.

nisha: thanks. if we can reproduce with a 2-3 prompt minimized case that's highest priority — will provision dev to test kernel patch.

sara: re-run queued on A100 pool (job 98321). I'll post outcomes here.

liam: posting interim minimal case (in thread gist). appears reproducible with 3 prompts. linking: https://gists.redwood/min_case_ev6592

maya: good progress. keep me posted. we can escalate to runtime oncall if patch looks non-trivial.

infra-bot: Reminder: add the alert tag `eng-runtime` to EV-6592 if runtime action taken.

liam: added tag and note to alert. next update in ~90m.
